title: Competing Concurrency-Control Mechanisms on a Single Resource
pattern: Accessing or protecting a shared resource using different concurrency or synchronization mechanisms in different parts of the system.
why_bad: It breaks the data safety guarantee. If even a single call site bypasses the lock or transaction convention, the entire resource is exposed to data races and memory corruption.
detection: Identify raw pointer, `unsafe`, or non-synchronized accesses to a static variable that is elsewhere protected by a standard mutex or lock wrapper.
counterexample: None. Mixing locked and lock-free writes on the same raw memory breaks safety. `Strong`.
fix: Encapsulate the raw resource completely, exposing only a synchronized API that forces all callers to acquire the lock.
source: *The Pragmatic Programmer, 20th Anniversary Edition* by Andrew Hunt and David Thomas (2019), p. 354.
